ruxen 0.2.1: security and compatibility fixes measured against nginx 1.30, runtime DNS (`resolver`), OCSP stapling, and a start on machines with many cores. ruxen is an experimental nginx-compatible HTTP server and reverse proxy written from scratch in Rust: Linux-only, HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2, thread-per-core on `io_uring` (monoio, epoll where `io_uring` is blocked), TLS via rustls.

> [!WARNING]
> This is an experimental release. It is not production-ready and is not a drop-in replacement for nginx.

**The reference version is now nginx 1.30**, the current stable branch, instead of 1.24.0: the performance contract (≥ 95% of nginx's throughput on every bench scenario) and the compatibility target both move to it. On the bench configurations nginx 1.30.6 and 1.24.0 run at the same speed (±1.3%). Against 1.30.6 on the i7, ruxen is at ≥ 95% on 91 of 94 scenarios, with a median of 121.5% ([`bench/campaign-2026-10-21`](https://github.com/gvozdetsky/ruxen/blob/v0.2.1/bench/campaign-2026-10-21/REPORT.md)). The behaviour 1.30 changed from 1.24 that ruxen doesn't follow yet has issues: the largest is nginx 1.29.7's upstream defaults (#582, planned for 0.2.2).

## Security

ruxen has no known production users yet; these were found by a review of nginx's changes from 1.24.0 to 1.30.6 and by an audit (#529), and fixed in the open. Upgrade from 0.2.0.

- **`location ~\.php$` with the modifier written against the pattern was a literal prefix** (#577). A `deny`, `return` or `proxy_pass` in such a location didn't apply, so the request fell through to another location: fail-open. The modifiers `=`, `^~`, `~` and `~*` are now read off the front of a single argument, as nginx does.
- **A bare LF or CR in a chunked request's trailer** let `0\r\n\n` swallow the next pipelined request as trailer lines (#578). It is a 400, as in nginx since 1.29.4.
- **An HTTP/2 request whose `:authority` and `Host` differ** is a 400, as in nginx since 1.29.1 (#592). ruxen routed by one and passed on the other.
- **`listen … quic`** opened a plaintext TCP listener on the port (#593). It is now ignored with a `[warn]`: ruxen has no HTTP/3, and a server whose only listen is `quic` gets no default `:80` either.
- **A cache hit was read whole into memory** before it was sent (#515); it is sent from the cache file.
- `location $var` is an `[emerg]` until predicate locations (nginx 1.31.5) exist (#596): accepted as a literal prefix, it never matched.

## Fixes

- **More than about 16 workers failed to start on Linux 7.0** (#612): every `io_uring` ring counts against the user's `RLIMIT_MEMLOCK` unless the process has `CAP_IPC_LOCK`, and a worker's 4096-entry ring is about 0.5 MiB of the common 8 MiB. `worker_processes auto` on a 32-thread machine failed with `io_uring_setup() failed (12: Cannot allocate memory)`, also under the shipped systemd unit. Each generation of workers now takes the largest ring that fits (4096, 1024 or 256 entries) with a `[warn]`, and the systemd unit sets `LimitMEMLOCK=128M`. A 1024-entry ring measures the same as a 4096-entry one.
- **A 103 Early Hints from the backend became the final response** and the client hung (#581). The interim heads are skipped, as nginx does without `early_hints`; an HTTP/1.0 103 is a 502.
- A worker panic now stops the server within 5 s and refuses new connections in the meantime (#495). SIGQUIT closes the listening sockets at once (#552).
- A client that closes a TLS connection while the upstream is awaited is noticed (#489). Back-to-back reloads no longer keep retired configurations in memory (#503). The ClientHello reader stops on end of file (#511).
- The 400 for a bad request and `100 Continue` are sent under `send_timeout` (#510).
- `set $args` replaces the request's arguments (#543).

## nginx compatibility

- **`resolver` and `resolver_timeout`** (#133): runtime DNS for a `proxy_pass` with variables that renders a host name. `valid=`, `ipv4=` and `ipv6=` work, answers are cached by their TTL, CNAMEs are followed and truncated answers are retried over TCP, and a name that doesn't resolve is a 502 with nginx's error-log line.
- **OCSP stapling** (#141, #560): `ssl_stapling`, `ssl_stapling_file`, `ssl_stapling_responder`, `ssl_stapling_verify`. The responder is resolved with `resolver` on each fetch, with a warning when there is none.
- **From nginx 1.25–1.30:**
  - `ssl_verify_client` with only `ssl_trusted_certificate` (#587);
  - realip takes a bracketed IPv6 address without a port (#583);
  - the default multi-range limit counts the multipart overhead (#588);
  - 407 has its reason phrase and error page (#591);
  - `http2_chunk_size`, `http2_push` and `http2_push_preload` are accepted in a location (#594).
- No TLS warning for a server that is TLS on another of its listens (#553).

## Install

Three prebuilt binaries, each also under a versioned name (`ruxen-v0.2.1-<target>.tar.gz`), with a `SHA256SUMS` file:

| tarball | for |
| --- | --- |
| `ruxen-x86_64-linux-gnu.tar.gz` | x86_64 with glibc 2.35 or newer |
| `ruxen-aarch64-linux-gnu.tar.gz` | ARM64 with glibc 2.35 or newer (Graviton, Ampere, Raspberry Pi 5 on a 64-bit OS) |
| `ruxen-x86_64-linux-musl.tar.gz` | any x86_64 Linux, static (Alpine, older glibc) |

```bash
curl -LO https://github.com/gvozdetsky/ruxen/releases/download/v0.2.1/ruxen-v0.2.1-x86_64-linux-gnu.tar.gz
sha256sum -c --ignore-missing SHA256SUMS   # after downloading SHA256SUMS from this release
tar xzf ruxen-v0.2.1-x86_64-linux-gnu.tar.gz
cd ruxen-v0.2.1-x86_64-linux-gnu
./ruxen -t -c "$PWD/examples/minimal.conf"
```

Container image, amd64 and arm64:

```bash
docker run --rm -p 8080:8080 ghcr.io/gvozdetsky/ruxen:0.2.1
curl http://127.0.0.1:8080/
```

It runs as an unprivileged user. Docker's default seccomp profile blocks `io_uring`, so under it ruxen runs on epoll; [`contrib/docker/seccomp-io_uring.json`](https://github.com/gvozdetsky/ruxen/blob/v0.2.1/contrib/docker/seccomp-io_uring.json) allows `io_uring` and nothing else beyond the default (`--security-opt seccomp=contrib/docker/seccomp-io_uring.json`). On a host with many cores, the container's memlock limit may need raising for `io_uring` (`--ulimit memlock=134217728`, #612). A hardened systemd unit and a logrotate snippet are in [`contrib/`](https://github.com/gvozdetsky/ruxen/tree/v0.2.1/contrib).

From crates.io (needs `cmake` and a C compiler for rustls's `aws-lc-rs` backend):

```bash
cargo install ruxen --locked
```

## Tests

nginx-tests: 172 of the 192 files that apply pass (0.2.0: 165 of 191), see [`NGINX_TEST_PROGRESS.md`](https://github.com/gvozdetsky/ruxen/blob/v0.2.1/NGINX_TEST_PROGRESS.md). Config corpus: ruxen loads 217 of 238 real-world configurations (91%).
